name: DHT12 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Aosong digital temperature (-20 to 60 °C, ±0.5 °C) and relative humidity (20–95 %, ±5 %) sensor, the I2C upgrade of the DHT11, with 0.1 unit resolution and an 8-bit sum checksum. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V; I2C up to 400 kHz; no pull-ups inside. Sold as: Aosong DHT12 bare 4-lead 2.54 mm sensor (VDD, SDA, GND, SCL), fixed I2C address 0x5C (0xB8 in 8-bit notation).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 2.7–5.5 V; use 3.3 V with ESP32/Pico so the I2C pull-ups go to 3.3 V

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data; needs an external pull-up (1–10 kΩ, e.g. 4.7 kΩ) to VDD

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock; needs an external pull-up (1–10 kΩ, e.g. 4.7 kΩ) to VDD. Held low at power-up, it selects the single-wire (DHT11-style) mode instead

buildNotes: Pins, looking at the slotted front, left to right: 1 VDD, 2 SDA, 3 GND, 4 SCL. The sensor has no pull-ups: fit 1–10 kΩ (e.g. 4.7 kΩ) from SDA and from SCL to VDD.
SCL must be high when the sensor powers up, otherwise it chooses single-wire mode until the next power cycle.

Read: write register address 0x00, repeated start, read 5 bytes: humidity integer, humidity tenths, temperature integer, temperature tenths (bit 7 = negative), checksum = low 8 bits of the sum of the first four.
Wait 2 s after power-up and read at most once every 2 s; each read returns the measurement taken at the previous read.
The address is fixed at 0x5C, so only one DHT12 can share a bus. Bus speed 400 kHz or less.

driver.code:
# DHT12 temperature & humidity sensor (Aosong DHT12), MicroPython driver for its I2C mode.
# Datasheet (section 8.1): I2C address 0xB8 in 8-bit notation = 0x5C (7-bit). Read sequence:
# START, DEV SEL + W, BYTE ADDR 0x00, repeated START, DEV SEL + R, 5 data bytes, NACK, STOP.
#   0x00 humidity integer, 0x01 humidity tenths, 0x02 temperature integer,
#   0x03 temperature tenths (bit 7 = 1 means the temperature is negative), 0x04 checksum.
# Checksum = (byte0 + byte1 + byte2 + byte3) & 0xFF.
# Bus speed 400 kHz max; SDA and SCL each need a 1-10 kOhm pull-up (the bare sensor has none).
# SCL must be high at power-up or the sensor chooses its single-wire (DHT11-style) mode.
# Wait 2 s after power-up; read at most once every 2 s. Each read returns the previous measurement.
import time

ADDR = 0x5C  # 0xB8 in the datasheet's 8-bit (address + R/W) notation


class DHT12:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def read(self):
        """Return (temperature in °C, relative humidity in %)."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, 0x00, 5)
        if (d[0] + d[1] + d[2] + d[3]) & 0xFF != d[4]:
            raise OSError('DHT12 checksum mismatch: check the wiring and pull-ups')
        h = d[0] + d[1] / 10
        t = d[2] + (d[3] & 0x7F) / 10
        if d[3] & 0x80:
            t = -t
        return t, h

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from dht12 import DHT12

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = DHT12(i2c)
time.sleep(2)  # datasheet: let the sensor settle for 2 s after power-up
while True:
    try:
        t, h = sensor.read()
        print('T=%.1fC H=%.1f%%' % (t, h))
    except OSError as e:
        print('DHT12 error:', e)
    time.sleep(2)
